Virginia’s housing & rental market Virginia’s housing market has a median sale price of $425K, reflecting steady valuations across the state. Sales pace has slowed, with median days on market up 20% year-over-year. Renters face a median monthly rent of $2.3K while active for-sale listings total 36.9K, suggesting more for-sale supply relative to recent periods. Virginia Quick Market Insights Price Per Square Foot: The median sale price per square foot is $230, giving buyers a clear benchmark for comparing neighborhoods and helping sellers set competitive list prices. Month-over-month Price Change: Median asking prices rose 1.19% month-over-month, a modest uptick that may strengthen seller negotiating positions if the trend continues. Rental Inventory: There are 10.0K rental listings, which provides renters with broader choice and can ease upward pressure on rents in markets with more available units. Year-over-year Rent Growth: Median rents increased 2.23% year-over-year, indicating steady rent inflation that affects renter affordability and investor expectations for income growth. Realtor.com’s market Hotness Index 72 Hot Virginia ranks #9 nationally and is highly active and strong. Homes sell in a median of 42 days. The Realtor.com Hotness Index measures how fast homes sell and how much demand they attract, ranking markets to spotlight the most competitive areas. It’s a timely tool for buyers and sellers to see where housing is heating up. What should someone consider when choosing a neighborhood in Virginia? Buyers and renters should evaluate commute times, school districts, property taxes, and local amenities when comparing Virginia neighborhoods. Realtor.com provides listings, neighborhood insights, and licensed agents to help streamline the local search. What are the current listing count, median price, and price per square foot in Virginia? As of the latest data, Virginia has 36,929 active listings with a median listing price of $425,000 and a median price per square foot of $230. These benchmarks help buyers and sellers assess market position and set competitive offers. How has Virginia’s market changed month-over-month? Month-over-month, Virginia’s for-sale inventory declined -0.76% while the median listing price rose 1.19% and the median price per square foot increased 1.77%. These month-over-month shifts indicate tightening supply with modest upward pressure on prices. What are the year-over-year trends in Virginia’s housing market? Year-over-year, Virginia’s for-sale count is up 8.83% while the median listing price and median price per square foot increased 1.19% and 2.22%, respectively. This year-over-year performance reflects expanding supply alongside modest price appreciation statewide. How has Virginia’s housing market changed over the past three years? Over three years, Virginia’s for-sale count rose 4.51%, median listing price increased 3.66%, and median price per square foot climbed 10.05%. The three-year changes show steady inventory gains with stronger per-square-foot appreciation. For sellers Sellers in Virginia face a market with a median for-sale price of $425K and 36.9K homes currently listed, signaling moderate inventory alongside solid pricing. On a month-over-month’ basis inventory ticked down -0.76% while the median list price rose 1.19%, median days on market shortened -25%, and price per square foot increased 1.77%, indicating faster sales and improving pricing momentum for sellers. Compared year-over-year’, listings are up 8.83%, days on market are longer by 20%, and price per square foot is higher by 2.22%, suggesting stronger annual demand but modestly slower turnover compared with last year.
